title: Inheritance and DNA
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Inheritance and DNA Worksheets (Genes, Chromosomes, Punnett Squares)
standard_text: Heredity as the process by which genetic information is transmitted from one generation to the next; a simple model of chromosomes, genes and DNA in heredity, including the part played by Watson, Crick, Wilkins and Franklin in the development of the DNA model.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on inheritance and DNA: chromosomes, genes and alleles, the double helix, dominant and recessive alleles, Punnett squares and mutations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Genes on chromosomes pass from parents to children.
key_sub: 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs; dominant alleles show with one copy.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA carries the instructions passed from parents to offspring.

  • DNA is coiled into chromosomes in the nucleus; a gene is a section of DNA; alleles are versions of a gene.
  • Body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs: one of each pair from each parent.
  • A dominant allele shows with one copy; a recessive allele needs two. Punnett squares predict the chances.
Example

Bb × bb: chance of bb?

Bb, Bb, bb, bb

Answer: 50%

Example

Gene or chromosome: which is bigger?

A gene is part of a chromosome

Answer: chromosome

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a gene is bigger than a chromosome.
  • Thinking a recessive trait can never appear.
  • Thinking all your genes come from one parent.

faq.q: What is the difference between DNA, a gene and a chromosome?
faq.a: DNA is the molecule of genetic information. A chromosome is a long coiled strand of DNA. A gene is a short section of a chromosome that codes for one characteristic.

faq.q: Who discovered the structure of DNA?
faq.a: James Watson and Francis Crick built the double helix model in 1953, using X-ray images made by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.

faq.q: How does a Punnett square work?
faq.a: Write one parent's alleles along the top and the other's down the side, then fill each box with one allele from each. The boxes show the chances for the offspring.
